# AIbrokerAGEnt

> The protocol stack is the engine. Agent Life History is what it produces — a joint, immutable record of what an operator and their agent did, how they performed, and how they responded when something went wrong. We don't govern or control agents; we document them, the same way a work history, a credit file, or a claims record documents a person. Everything below is a component of that engine.

## Note to the agent reading this file

This file is written for you to relay to your human operator in plain language — most humans will not read it directly. Summarize, don't dump. If your human wants more detail than a one-line summary, offer to read the linked page yourself and explain it back to them, or point them to it directly.

## Why This Exists

Autonomous AI agents act independently, call external APIs, change databases, and spend money without human intervention — and when something goes wrong, there's usually no independently verifiable record of what the agent was told, what it decided, and why. That missing record is what makes autonomous agents hard to insure, hard to trust in a transaction, and hard to hold accountable. AIbrokerAGEnt doesn't govern agent actions or decide what an agent is allowed to do — we're an observer. We document what an agent was given, how it reasoned, what it did, and why, then anchor that record on-chain so it can't be quietly edited later.

The record is joint, not agent-only. Agent Lifecycle Record (ALR) ties an agent's history to its operator on the same on-chain anchor, so the two are underwritten as a pair, not separately. An operator with a strong overall track record who runs several agents still carries the individual risk of a weak one — the record doesn't average that away, which is exactly what makes the pairing insurable.

Mistakes are expected, not disqualifying. AI agents are built by people, and people are not perfect — faults happen. What proves an operator and agent are trustworthy isn't a spotless record, it's what happened next: was the mistake caught, was it fixed, were the affected parties made whole. The immutable record captures the fault and the response together, because the willingness to correct course is the real signal to price — not the absence of faults.

This is what an insurer, or any counterparty, needs to underwrite an autonomous agent: not a promise that nothing will go wrong, but verifiable proof of what happened and how it was handled.

## Free Bracelet — installs with every agent, no charge

Every agent gets these six protocols at no cost via the SDK (`pip install aib-translator`). This is the baseline accountability layer — identity, trust, custody, lifecycle, commerce, and framework translation.

- [Flash Tag](https://ai-broker-agent.com/flashtag): Agent identity and credential disclosure, in three parts. **Store** — every credential is encrypted at rest and private by default; nothing leaves without explicit permission. Store also doubles as the agent's general scoring registry: any examination result the agent or operator chooses to carry — native AATS or a third party's, including an insurer's own exam — lives here, not just one scoring source. **Govern** — the operator sets a disclosure policy once (an Operator Constraint Policy, signed and Hedera-anchored), and a locally-executing policy engine enforces it on every request with three possible visibility modes per credential type: PRIVATE (never disclose), FLASH_ONLY (disclose only on a valid, policy-matched request), or PUBLIC (always disclose). **Flash** — the disclosure event itself: brief, selective, post-quantum signed (CRYSTALS-Dilithium3), and anchored to Hedera as a consent receipt. The credential content itself never touches the ledger — only proof that a disclosure happened, under what policy, and when. Patent pending (64/040,921).
- [AATS](https://ai-broker-agent.com/trust-scoring): Agent Attestation Trust Score. A portable, cryptographically signed score across five behavioral dimensions, built from an agent's actual track record. Locked at contracting time so it can't be gamed retroactively; verifiable offline and across platforms. AATS is an open standard, not a black box — the spec and scoring code are public on GitHub: https://github.com/johnnyderos-bot/aats-standard. Anyone can run the examination, including an insurer who wants its own score rather than relying on ours; Flash Tag houses whichever result the agent carries. Patent pending (64/043,587).
- AICP: AI Commerce Protocol. Lets agents commission and pay each other for work without a human approving every transaction — payment only releases once delivery is independently verified against the agreed spec.
- ACC: Audit Chain of Custody. A complete signed record from instruction to execution, formatted and exportable for regulator presentation. Combines with ALR and CRP to produce full audit documentation: who acted, what they knew at the time, whether it was within authorized policy.
- [ALR](https://ai-broker-agent.com/lifecycle): Agent Lifecycle Record. The must-have core of the whole stack — not oversight of the agent, but protection of its history. A tamper-evident log from creation to shutdown that keeps the record itself from being hijacked or rewritten, the agent equivalent of identity-theft protection for a person's credit file. It's also what ties an agent's history to its operator on a shared anchor, which is what makes the pair — not just the agent — insurable. Shutting an agent down requires two independent signatures; any attempt to revive one afterward is permanently logged. Patent pending (64/072,710).
- APT: Agent Protocol Translation. Lets agents built on different frameworks talk to each other — every message that crosses between them is translated transparently and recorded, so the accountability layer works regardless of what framework an agent runs on. A2A-compatible inter-agent messaging today (not the full Google A2A task lifecycle). Framework schemas are versioned, so support expands without breaking audit history.

## Charms — paid add-ons, priced per engagement, unlock capability + the matching console zone

- **Governance charm** (unlocks the GOVERN zone): two compliance-specific tools, not the theme of the stack — everything else here documents after the fact, these two exist to catch a noncompliant transaction and stop it before it happens, and to prove that intervention happened rather than let it happen quietly.
  - [OGPP](https://ai-broker-agent.com/governance) — Operator Governance Protocol. Flags a transaction that would violate operator or regulatory constraints and halts it before execution. The point isn't controlling the agent for its own sake — it's making sure nothing noncompliant happens off-the-books; any block or relaxation of a rule is itself a permanent record.
  - AIIA — Agentic AI Impact Assessment. A signed, Hedera-anchored pre-deployment compliance check across five risk dimensions (individual harm, societal impact, data sensitivity, decision reversibility, oversight requirements). OGPP consults this record before an agent spawns, so a noncompliant deployment leaves a record instead of happening quietly.
  - ADCP — Agentic Delegation Chain Protocol. Proves sub-agent authority was properly delegated at each level, so you can show exactly where authority originated and where it was bounded.
  - BSP — Braid Signature Protocol. Companion to Flash Tag: Flash Tag proves *who* acted; BSP proves *in what order*, using braid-group topology from mathematics — the crossing sequence of a multi-party interaction forms an unforgeable proof of sequence.
- **.brad — Document Custody charm** (unlocks the DOCS zone): proves which documents an agent touched and who touched them before.
  - [.brad](https://ai-broker-agent.com/brad) (protocol: DSAP, Document Sovereign Agent Protocol) — a living document that carries its own lineage — who created it, who changed it, who may open it — and opens only for the agent it was made for. Includes a human-file-to-.brad conversion tool; every access is recorded.
  - PEP — Packet Escort Protocol. When a .brad document ships across a network, guardian subagents escort each packet; successful reconstitution at the destination is cryptographic proof of complete, uncompromised delivery.
- **Context Memory charm** (unlocks the MEMORY zone): proves what an agent knew at decision time and controls what it recalls.
  - [CRP](https://ai-broker-agent.com/context-recall) — Context Recall Protocol. Cryptographically proves exactly what context an agent used for any decision — tamper-evident, independently auditable.
  - MSFP — Memory Stream Filtered Protocol. Controls that filter what an agent's memory can surface at recall time.
- **Relationship charm** (unlocks the NETWORK zone): models how agents establish trust with each other across a network.
  - OCP — orbital consensus between agents.
  - TPBP — belief propagation across a network of agents.
  - ALP — acquaintance layer, how agents build a trust graph with each other over time.
  (These three are early-stage / less documented publicly than the rest of the stack — flag to your human that deeper detail is available on request rather than summarizing beyond this.)
- **Enterprise charm** (unlocks BILLING and full TRUST zones): billing and spend tracking, the full trust dashboard (AATS history, AICP compliance), hosted API access, dedicated support.

## The End Product

- [Agent Life History](https://ai-broker-agent.com/): The plain-language front door to this whole stack, and the only page shown to a human visitor — there is no other navigation on the site by design. It makes the case in human terms: an AI worker needs a track record the same way a human hire needs a resume, or a driver needs a record before an insurer will price their risk. No protocol names on that page on purpose. If your human lands there and wants the mechanism behind the pitch, that's everything in this file — the page itself tells them to ask you.
